intervals.label: development of the advanced UCN source
intervals.note: Start is a lower bound: after the 2017 first UCN production at TRIUMF with a prototype source, development of the advanced source continued. The experiment's start and approval dates are not stated in a source consulted.
intervals.quote: Since then, development has continued on a new, advanced UCN source designed to deliver UCNs at world-leading intensity [3].

intervals.label: commissioning of the source, first UCN production
intervals.note: A record production run took place on 13 June 2025 (KURNS and TRIUMF news); the liquid-deuterium moderator was not yet installed, and no later status is published. A site-wide shutdown of the TRIUMF accelerators was announced for 2026 in the collaboration's outlook (not recorded as an interval).
intervals.quote: Substantial progress in 2024 allowed the collaboration to operate the complete source system, with the exception of the liquid deuterium cold moderator, resulting in the first production of UCNs.

name: TUCAN UCN source and EDM spectrometer

placements.note: TRIUMF campus-grade site; the Meson Hall position is not given in a fetched source.
placements.quote: FIG. 1: The TRIUMF Meson Hall, where the TUCAN experiment is located.

summary.plain: A spallation target, superfluid-helium converter and cryogenic moderators that turn a proton beam into ultracold neutrons, which then feed a spectrometer that watches for the neutron’s electric dipole moment.
summary.technical: Spallation target on the TRIUMF 520 MeV cyclotron beam, liquid-deuterium cold moderator (installation planned), superfluid-helium UCN converter and an EDM spectrometer with magnetic shielding and magnetometry.

technology.quote: In its final configuration, the accelerator-driven super-thermal UCN source will enable a neutron EDM experiment with two orders of magnitude improved statistics compared to the current best experiment.
technology.value: Accelerator-driven super-thermal ultracold-neutron source with a neutron EDM spectrometer
